correctness.rationale: For every nontrivial hypersimplex, coordinate-fixing classifies all faces. Joint block symmetrization and one-violation mass inequality give exact squared distance n/[n(a+b)-(a-b)^2] for every nonvertex face, with an explicit uniform vertex-mixture attaining the relaxation. Vertex distances are n/[k(n-k)] and strictly larger for the stated ranks. A monotone-in-b and concave-in-a integer optimization proves the two formula branches and the complete parity-dependent optimizing face types. Exact rational checks cover 465 rank pairs and 50,840 face-orbits; independent small-dimensional direct convex quadratic minimizations support the proof but are not used as an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The exact hypersimplex pyramidal-width classification, including its phase change in minimizing face dimensions, was compared by mathematical implication with published facial-distance results and standard hypersimplex face enumeration. The 2026 universal bound of Deza et al. and the calculus/lower bounds of Peña--Wirth do not determine the exact intermediate-rank value or minimizing faces. Ferroni--Schröter enumerates faces, not their separation distances. Targeted terminology and semantic-record searches found no covering result, but lack of a hit is not a novelty proof and residual priority risk is disclosed.
residual_risks: The later Birkhoff-focused pages and appendices of arXiv:2609.32440 were not fully accessible in the current reader; no claim of whole-document negative coverage is made.
Older Frank-Wolfe condition-number and uniform-matroid literature might use an equivalent normalization or another name; exhaustive historical priority is not certified.

The 2025 product-polytope paper was not fully inspected; its published abstract and excerpt are not a whole-document novelty clearance. Nontrivial hypersimplices are not products, reducing direct-overlap plausibility.

value.rationale: Facial distance/pyramidal width is a natural quantitative polytope condition measure appearing in linear-convergence guarantees for Frank--Wolfe variants. Hypersimplices are the canonical uniform-matroid base polytopes and standard non-product 0/1 polytopes. A complete sharp value and classification of minimizing faces for every intermediate rank, including a structural edge-to-higher-dimensional phase transition, goes beyond general estimates and has plausible direct value in optimization geometry.
